evals.prompt: Package my finished crate as a BagIt zip I can hand to the archive.
evals.expected_output: bagit.txt, manifest listing every payload file including the metadata, crate under data/.
expectations: Crate files are placed under data/

evals.prompt: Our Rails catalogue has a page per training material and already embeds Bioschemas JSON-LD. Add FAIR Signposting so machines can find an RO-Crate for each record.
evals.expected_output: Link header and HTML <link> with describedby (RO-Crate profile), cite-as, author, license, type; crate URL plus content negotiation; signposts first and framework preload links quoted; tested with the signposting library and rocrate-validator.
expectations: Advertises the crate with rel="describedby", type="application/ld+json" and profile="https://w3id.org/ro/crate"
Sends the same links in the HTTP Link header and as HTML <link> elements
Warns that the framework's own Link entries (Rails preload with unquoted integrity values or nopush) can make strict parsers reject the whole header, and puts the signposting links first
Keeps plain application/ld+json returning the existing JSON-LD and serves the crate for the RO-Crate profile
Uses rel="item" only for downloadable content, not for HTML pages
Suggests testing with an independent client (Python signposting) and validating the returned crate
